title: Quick Accent not remembering frequent accents after restart (persists after 0.94 fix)

judgment.rationale: Usage data is saved at shutdown, but the current hard-exit path explicitly skips saving.
evidence: IncrementUsageFrequency mutates memory and Save is normally called during disposal.
Program.Terminate can call Environment.Exit when the dispatcher queue is unavailable.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve write-through atomic persistence and process-boundary tests.

fix_assessment.rationale: The prior fix added persistence but does not cover the documented hard-exit path.

proposed_fixes.title: Persist usage ordering before shutdown
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Quick Accent holds usage counters in memory until shutdown, so sign-out, dispatcher races, and hard exits can discard the updated ordering.
plan: Save immediately after IncrementUsageFrequency when sorting is enabled.
Use atomic temporary-file replacement in CharactersUsageInfo.Save.
Add reload and real process-boundary tests.
verification: Use a character repeatedly, restart the module, and verify it remains first.
Cover malformed JSON, write failure, sorting disabled, and shutdown fallback.

confidence.rationale: The source documents the unsaved exit path and matches the symptom, but a current process-boundary repro is still desirable.

issue_context.summary: Quick Accent's usage-frequency ordering can reset after sign-out or restart because updates remain in memory until shutdown.
known_information: The original fix was intended to persist usage frequency.
Comments reproduce the reset on 0.100.2 and after reboot/sign-out.
The UI disposal path saves, but Program.Terminate has an Environment.Exit fallback that does not.
inferences: Shutdown-only persistence likely loses the latest usage data during session teardown or dispatcher failure.
Atomic replacement is needed to avoid corrupting the previous valid file.
issue_context.analysis: Immediate UI-thread persistence is a narrow robustness fix that preserves the existing setting semantics while covering the documented loss path.
initial_investigation: Inspected CharactersUsageInfo, PowerAccent, MainWindow disposal, Program.Terminate, unit tests, and E2E helpers.
Confirmed no process-boundary persistence test exists.

information_gaps.information: A current reproduction that distinguishes a normal restart from sign-out, shutdown, or abrupt PowerToys termination.
information_gaps.why_needed: It confirms that the documented persistence-loss path still reaches the hard-exit boundary and determines the focused process-boundary regression case.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Use one accent repeatedly, test normal module restart and Windows sign-out or shutdown separately, then report which path loses the ordering and the current PowerToys version.

design.root_cause: Usage frequency is incremented in memory and normally written only by SaveUsageInfo during disposal; Environment.Exit bypasses disposal.
evidence: Program.Terminate documents a hard-exit fallback without saving.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Increment updates memory; persistence waits for shutdown.
implementation_steps.change: Save immediately after increment when sorting is enabled, without blocking insertion on write failure.
edge_cases: Log write failures and preserve character insertion.
tests: Increment then construct a new store and verify the counter/order.

implementation_steps.change: Write a unique temporary file and atomically replace the prior file.
implementation_steps.code_block: write temp; flush/close; replace destination; clean temp on failure.
edge_cases: Preserve prior valid data on failure.
Avoid collisions and stale temp cleanup.
tests: Simulate replacement/write failure and verify previous JSON remains valid.

implementation_steps.code_block: use character; stop process; start process; trigger same letter; assert prior frequent character is first.
edge_cases: Use existing test helpers and avoid parallel UI tests.
tests: Run the existing Core and UI test projects.

verify: Build PowerAccent Core and UI tests in x64 Debug.
Restart the module after repeated use and verify ordering survives.
risks: Per-selection I/O may add latency; debounce only after measuring.
A write failure must not break input.
alternatives: Periodic saves reduce I/O but still lose recent data.
Session-event-only saves do not protect against crashes or hard exit.

actions.label: Approve Quick Accent persistence design
actions.note: Fork-side implementation only; no upstream action.

actions.label: Request current restart and sign-out reproduction

comment.body: The current design targets usage ordering that is held in memory until shutdown, including a hard-exit fallback. To focus the regression coverage, please test the latest PowerToys version after using one accent repeatedly and report separately whether its ordering resets after a normal module restart, Windows sign-out, shutdown, or another abrupt termination.

actions.note: Draft only; no upstream comment is posted without explicit approval.

non_blocking_notes: Validate write-through performance and a real process boundary.
